subject.title: Voice & Audio Assistant requires an unbundled developer backend checkout

question: Should the Windows installer ship and maintain an Assistant backend runtime, or should the Voice & Audio Assistant be unavailable until a supported backend is configured?
rationale: The report establishes a broken visible flow, but choosing packaged runtime ownership versus a disabled capability determines the long-term installer, support, and update contract.

options.title: Gate the control on supported runtime availability
options.body: Disable or hide Start Assistant when no supported packaged or configured runtime is present, with an in-product explanation and a supported setup route.

options.title: Package the Assistant runtime
options.body: Bundle and maintain the required backend with the Windows installer, including upgrade, size, security, and offline-install validation.

recommendation.title: Gate the control on supported runtime availability
recommendation.body: Disable or hide Start Assistant when no supported packaged or configured runtime is present, with an in-product explanation and a supported setup route.
